Tested first, and it FAILED: on five years of NSE’s own NIFTY data, selling NIFTY in these downtrends made +0.29% a trade in the final year — 18 trades, t = 0.205, no different from nothing (the test was fixed before it was run). Calls — you BUY the call, it pays if the stock RISES

If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹18,55,193 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹9,34,045 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 83 rows are on 12 stocks: several strikes of one stock are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Healthcare 31, Financial Services 21, Consumer Services 7. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a call is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹8,316.68 across all 83 rows, one lot each, plus the bid-ask spread, which is not known without a live book (83 of these rows). 70 of 83 are priced above the stock’s own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the BUY signal works, and it failed: the desk’s own rating, replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, made −0.028% a trade on its BUY and ACCUMULATE rows (32,725 trades, 36.7% winners).

Puts — you BUY the put, it pays if the index or stock FALLS

If you take every row here (one lot each): ₹53,35,511 in total; if every stop is hit, −₹26,86,511 — more if prices gap through the stops.
These 250 rows are on 27 names: several strikes of one name are one bet, not several. Most rows are in: Index 139, Financial Services 28, Metals & Mining 14. Rows in one sector tend to fall together. With no trend and fairly priced options, a put is expected to lose about its charges: about −₹24,451.34 across all 250 rows, one lot each, plus the bid-ask spread, which is not known without a live book (250 of these rows). 237 of 250 are priced above their own recent movement (implied above realised), which makes it worse. They make money only if the fall continues, and selling NIFTY in these downtrends failed its pre-registered test (final year t = 0.205).
BAD-DAY RISK, every row together — 1 day in 20: −₹15,95,720 or worse · worst day: −₹39,01,146 · market opens 5% higher: −₹42,26,145
Today’s 250 rows (one lot each) replayed through each of the last 500 trading days, Tue, 8 Oct 2024 to Tue, 6 Oct 2026, on real prices, with every stop and target in the market. Not a forecast: these are days that already happened. Before charges.
1 day in 20: on the worst 25 of those 500 days, all the rows together lost at least ₹15,95,720 — ₹21,56,523 on average.
Worst day, Tue, 3 Feb 2026 (NIFTY +2.55%): 26 of 27 names rose and 239 stops were hit, 200 of them by a gap at the open — a loss of −₹39,01,146, against −₹26,67,184 if every stop had filled at its own price (before charges).
Market opens 5% higher: −₹42,26,145. Each name opens higher by its own measured sensitivity to NIFTY (median 1.12), and a stop fills at the open, not at its own price.
Together: on those 25 worst days, 91.2% of the names rose at once. These rows are closer to one bet on the market than to 27 separate ones.
Most of the bad-day loss: NIFTY 29.7%, BANKNIFTY 21.4%, MIDCPNIFTY 10.9%, FINNIFTY 4.8%, AUBANK 4.3%.
Demergers, bonuses and splits are read from NSE’s own filings (Wed, 7 Oct 2026), so none of them counts as a crash.
For puts these figures are the OPTIMISTIC end. Each put is repriced with Black-76 at its own implied volatility, held where it is — but a put loses on the days the market rises, and on those days implied volatility usually falls, which takes still more off a put (India VIX moved −7% on Tue, 3 Feb 2026). The real loss on such a day can be larger than shown.
The stock puts lean on the desk’s SELL and REDUCE ratings, and those were tested: shorting them LOST. Replayed on six years of NSE’s prices, shorting every SELL/REDUCE row on this desk’s limit, target and stop made −0.139% a trade (35,236 trades, t = −3.31 — reliably negative), and over 20 sessions those stocks did slightly BETTER than the market. They are shown because you asked for the falling names, not because the rating picks fallers.
Looked for on NIFTY, BANKNIFTY, FINNIFTY, MIDCPNIFTY, NIFTYNXT50 and on the 54 stocks rated SELL or REDUCE that are falling themselves; 27 had contracts that cleared every gate, the indices first. One side per name, the side the market’s direction points to.

Hit rate counts only trades that filled and then finished. IF RANDOM is how often the target would come before the stop if prices moved at random — each trade's break-even, before charges. Only a hit rate above it, over enough separate bets, is evidence of an edge. The touch odds the desk showed ignore the stop, so they always run higher. Futures returns are GROSS per unit; options are NET of every charge per lot. ALL has no average return (futures move about 1.5%, options about 50%), and its money is options net a lot plus futures at 20 units, gross.

HOW THIS IS SCORED. Every price this page freezes is bought on paper at the moment it is shown. Each build then checks the market, using the day’s high and low so a move between two builds is not missed. Every ambiguity counts against the record: a target and a stop in the same window is a stop; a target in the same window as the fill is not counted; a gap through the stop exits at the open; a fill is always at the limit, never better; a price from before the level was shown can never fill it. Unfilled day orders die at 15:30. Futures are held at most 20 sessions; options until expiry. Stored in the private repository under docs/ledger/, committed on every build, and copied to the Google Sheet.
WHERE THESE PRICES COME FROM. All prices are from the 2026-10-07 settlement file. The market was in its pre-open when this was built, so nothing here is executable right now. Premiums and the futures prices they are measured against both come from that same settlement file, so they describe the same moment. Not checked against NSE on this build (before the open, NSE's quote pages still show the previous session). Broker login OK from the build server at 2026-10-08 02:17 IST — a NIFTY quote came back. F&O ban for 2026-10-08: AMBUJACEM, BANDHANBNK, LICHSGFIN, SAIL — left out entirely, because NSE allows only exits in a banned stock. This page is a snapshot, rebuilt on a schedule — it is not a live feed. Check the price on your broker before placing anything. Net figures are after brokerage, STT at 0.15%, exchange, stamp and GST; the spread is extra and is only known where a live book was seen.
NO SHOCK SHIELD. Nothing on this page stops buys on a bad global morning — not a GIFT Nifty gap, a crude or S&P move, or an India VIX spike. Those signals were tested on NSE’s own data and failed (or had too few events to test), so they do not gate anything. Check the market yourself before acting on a shock day.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That any of it makes money. The paper ledger has 1142 resolved trade(s) so far — far too few for a measured hit rate — and every test fixed in advance so far, on data never used to build the rule, found no edge: the desk's own rating (replayed on six years of NSE data: −0.03% a trade on its buys, and its SELL/REDUCE shorts LOST −0.14% a trade, t = −3.3), 12-1 momentum, time-series momentum, low volatility, a 10-month market trend filter, and the NIFTY trend reader that now chooses between buys and puts (selling NIFTY in its downtrends: final year t = 0.21) — all six FAIL. The ranking is built on things that were measured, which is not the same as an edge that was proven. Size accordingly.
